# Side-by-side check against the real xfig (W22)

**Status:** 2026-10-25, first report: 97 scenarios, none failed to run. Generated by `cargo xtask xfig-compare` (see [development.md](development.md)); the HTML with the images is `target/xfig-compare/index.html` (not committed, regenerate it). Reviewed by reading the worst-scoring and one image of each kind of scenario; the `.fig` object differences are complete for the scenarios that save.

**Setup:** real xfig 3.2.9a (`/opt/homebrew/bin/xfig`, default options, scratch `HOME`) headless on `Xvfb :77`, window 1400x1000, zoom 1.0 (80 px/in); RustFig 1400 pt wide at zoom 1, light theme, Fig (0,0) at the canvas corner. Clicks are snapped to 1/16 inch (75 Fig units) so both apps' pixel origins give the same Fig point. The RustFig window is clipped to the screen height (826 pt on the test Mac), so its bottom bar sits higher than xfig's; scores for the whole window therefore start at about 0.23 and for the canvas crop at about 0.08 for any scenario (layout, background, antialiasing): compare scores between scenarios, not with zero.

**Method:** each scenario selects a mode (xfig: mouse on the mode button as in `w_modepanel.c`'s grid, RustFig: its accessible label), clicks the same Fig points, screenshots both, and where it changes the drawing saves both `.fig` files. Text height/length are not compared (fonts), nor xfig's radius -1 against 0 on non-box polylines.

**Coverage this round:** all 40 mode buttons selected (message, mouse-button hints, indicator panel); one object drawn with each drawing mode except picture and library (dialogs only); move, copy, delete, flip up/down and left/right, rotate cw/ccw, scale, move/add/delete point, update, convert, add arrow, and the edit panel of a box, circle, polyline and text; the five menus open; the pop-ups of line width, style, fill style, pen/fill colour, depth, join, cap, grid, point position, zoom, arrow mode/type/size, text justification/angle/flags/size/font. Not yet: second-level menu entries and dialogs behind them (Export, Open, Global settings, Set units, ...), compounds (glue/break/open), align, join/split, chop, tangent and the measure modes' effects, picture, library placement, text editing keys, middle/right buttons, Shift/Ctrl variants, other fixtures (arrows, fills, splines, metric), zoom and scroll.

## Differences

**intended** = a modern alternative CLAUDE.md allows or a decision recorded elsewhere; **real** = RustFig should change (task id proposed; `W22-n` are new rows to add to `docs/plan.md` when taken up).

### Drawn and edited objects (`.fig` output)

| # | Difference | Seen in | Verdict | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Interpolated splines are written with shape factor -1; xfig uses -0.5 (`object.h`: `S_SPLINE_INTERP`). The curve is visibly rounder than xfig's for the same points; same for line to spline conversion. | draw-interp-spline, draw-closed-interp-spline, edit-convert | **fixed 2026-10-25** | W22-1: use -0.5 for new interpolated splines and conversions (check the renderer reads -0.5 as fig2dev does) |
| 2 | Rotate about the clicked point: xfig rotates about the point under the pointer (or the centre set with the right button); RustFig about the object's bounding-box centre. | edit-rotate-cw, edit-rotate-ccw | **fixed 2026-10-25** | W22-2 (the click itself; xfig uses the nearest control point of the object): pivot at the click unless a centre was set (`e_rotate.c` `init_rotateobject`) |
| 3 | Moved and scaled objects keep their place in the file; xfig removes and re-appends them, so they draw on top of the others of the same depth. | edit-move, edit-scale (copy and update fine) | **fixed 2026-10-25** | W22-3: re-append moved/scaled objects as xfig does |
| 4 | New plain boxes, polygons and polylines are written with corner radius 7 (the arc-box default); xfig writes -1. Harmless to xfig and fig2dev, but not xfig's file. | draw-box, draw-polygon, draw-polyline, draw-regpoly | **fixed 2026-10-25** | W22-4 (regular polygons get 0 as `create_regpoly`): radius -1 for everything but arc-boxes (`tools/mod.rs` Box, `Polyline::new` default 7) |
| 5 | Circle/ellipse by radius and by diameter store centre and radius plus end points computed from them; xfig stores the clicked points (start and end). Same shape; diameter centre rounds up (10988) where xfig truncates (10987). | draw-circle-radius, draw-circle-diameter | **fixed 2026-10-25** | W22-5: keep the clicked points in start/end |
| 6 | Regular polygon: same vertices, opposite order (RustFig clockwise from the click, xfig the other way). | draw-regpoly | **fixed 2026-10-25** | W22-6 |
| 7 | Arc-box points start at the second corner and run on in xfig; RustFig starts at the first corner. A plain box starts like xfig's. | draw-arcbox | **fixed 2026-10-25** | W22-7 |
| 8 | Text height and length in the file differ (fonts of the machine). | draw-text and every scenario that saves | **intended** | fonts are the system's, F1 |
| 9 | Hairlines (thickness 1) are antialiased grey in RustFig, black one-pixel in xfig; object shapes, positions and text agree otherwise to the pixel. | all canvases | **intended** | CLAUDE.md: thickness drawn as fig2dev draws it (1/160 inch) |

### Not a difference

Flip up/down and left/right, copy, delete, update, move/add/delete point and add arrow give the same `.fig` objects in both apps; box, circle, polyline, spline, polygon, arc and text drawn with the default attributes give the same coordinates (after snapping) and attributes; the five menus have xfig's entries in xfig's order; the Snap menu is identical.
